newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down in dull trading on Thursday due to profit-taking after sharp gains over the past few days, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,740 yuan ($2,412) per tonne, losing 60 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,880 and hit a low of 20,600.
Janaury fell 100 to 20,250, February 100 to 20,450, March 150 to 20,630, May 80 to 20,720 and June 90 to 20,700.
Combined volume fell sharply to 44,900 tonnes from 82,650.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices steadily down for most of the session.
Traders said profit-taking was the main reason for today's falls and that copper was likely to continue to rise in the short term.
"Some wary investors liquidated their long positions at high levels but thin volume indicated many investors were optimistic about the market trend," one trader said.
"There was no trading on the London Metal Exchange for the Christmas holiday, which made some investors take a wait-and-see attitude," he added.

"Market sentiment has improved a lot due to sharp gains over the past few days and the fact later-maturing contracts stood firmly above the 20,500-yuan level gave long positions more confidence," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to rise further if it can stand above the 20,500-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up. January rose 10 to 13,960 yuan per tonne and February 100 to 14,300.
Combined volume rose to 1,550 tonnes from 430.
